_comment: Usage class per (file, enclosing function) for every D3D8 Lock/Unlock site the
engine has.  `d3d8-lock-scan.py --check` fails if a lock site is in no class or a
class entry matches no lock site, so adding a lock site forces a decision about
which Vulkan resource path has to serve it.
`contract` is what the *caller* relies on, i.e. what the Vulkan implementation must

classes.name: whole-surface write
classes.contract: lock a whole surface or mip level with no flags, fill every texel from the CPU, unlock; nothing is read back. Upload can happen entirely at unlock.
classes.vulkan: persistent host-visible staging allocation per resource + vkCmdCopyBufferToImage at unlock

classes.name: partial-rect write
classes.contract: same as C1, but the lock covers a sub-rect and the caller only writes inside it; texels outside the rect must survive.
classes.vulkan: as C1, but the copy region is the locked rect, and the staging allocation must hold the resource's current contents (not be discarded)

classes.name: read-back
classes.contract: D3DLOCK_READONLY on a surface, read the texels on the CPU, unlock. The data must be what the GPU last wrote.
classes.vulkan: vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer + queue submit + fence wait before Lock returns, i.e. a full pipeline stall

classes.name: mip-chain load, lock held across frames and threads
classes.contract: lock every mip level (or cube face, or volume slice) of a fresh texture at once, keep the pointers and pitches in an array, fill them later - for the background loader, on another thread and some frames later - then unlock them all.
classes.vulkan: one persistent host-visible staging allocation per texture covering all levels, mapped for the whole task lifetime, uploaded level by level at Unlock_Surfaces on the render thread

classes.name: dynamic ring stream
classes.contract: every frame, many times per frame: lock a sub-range of a dynamic vertex/index buffer with D3DLOCK_DISCARD (offset 0, buffer is renamed) or D3DLOCK_NOOVERWRITE (append, previously submitted draws still read the earlier bytes), write, unlock, draw.
classes.vulkan: per-frame linear allocator over a host-visible ring, frames-in-flight copies, no barriers between NOOVERWRITE sub-allocations; DISCARD advances to a fresh region rather than reusing bytes the GPU may still be reading

classes.name: static buffer fill
classes.contract: lock a static vertex/index buffer (whole, or a caller-chosen sub-range for the Append locks), write geometry once at load time, unlock, then draw from it for the rest of the level.
classes.vulkan: staging buffer + vkCmdCopyBuffer into a DEVICE_LOCAL buffer at unlock, or a persistently mapped host-visible buffer where BAR memory is available

classes.name: pointer kept after unlock
classes.contract: lock, unlock immediately, and keep using the returned pBits/Pitch for the rest of the process: the shroud writes into that pointer every frame and then CopyRects the surface to a texture. Undefined behaviour in D3D8 that happens to work for D3DPOOL_SYSTEMMEM.
classes.vulkan: the staging allocation for that surface must be permanently mapped and never recycled, and the upload has to be driven by the CopyRects that follows rather than by Unlock

classes.name: opaque hand-out
classes.contract: SurfaceClass::Lock/Unlock returns the raw pointer and pitch to arbitrary engine code, which may read, write, or both; the class cannot tell which. Callers outside the scanner's scope (GUI, map preview, water, terrain) use it.
classes.vulkan: read-write mapping: read-back on Lock (C3 cost) and upload on Unlock (C1 cost), unless each caller is audited and split into C1/C2/C3

classes.name: surface-to-surface convert, two locks held at once
classes.contract: the off-Windows D3DX substitute (D3DXLoadSurfaceFromSurface, and D3DXFilterTexture through it) locks two surfaces at the same time: the source with D3DLOCK_READONLY and reads every texel of it on the CPU, the destination with no flags and writes every texel inside the destination rect, converting format between the two. Both pointers have to be valid simultaneously, the source data must be what the GPU last wrote, and when the destination rect is a sub-rect the texels outside it must survive. In the D3DXFilterTexture case the two surfaces are consecutive mip levels of the SAME texture.
classes.vulkan: the source costs a read-back (C3: vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer + fence wait before Lock returns) and the destination a contents-preserving staging upload at unlock (C2), both inside one call; because the mip case locks two levels of one image, the per-resource staging allocation must be addressable per level so that reading level n-1 and writing level n do not alias
